blockers.title: Disclosing post-boot kernel replacement does not close the mandatory Linux OS-ABI member
evidence: The carried exact-byte-delivery requirement says the signed closure declares the platform base/host-ABI TCB, a closed allowlist and identity rule covers every permitted OS ABI, undeclared resolution or identity drift refuses, and hostile clean machines prove no ambient system dependency enters silently.

The contract taxonomy includes OS ABI, Linux remains mandatory in D-002 slice 1, and pathlessClasses requires the Linux OS-ABI signed entry to use PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED. A kernel M entered after the measured firmware launch implements the host ABI seen by the qualification process and is therefore an actual OS-ABI TCB member, regardless of the narrower label assigned to the boot-time K package.

NT-TCB-1 says an undeclared object on an active complete profile refuses and that inability to observe it requires qualification failure or a platform-removal path. v32 instead defines NT-TCB-DISCLOSE-KEXEC as not a pass/fail cell, permits later M to be outside the bind, forbids treating the gap as NT-TCB-1 inapplicability, and also forbids treating it as a Linux withdrawal. Those clauses leave no route by which the mandatory NT-TCB-1 OS-ABI cell can pass.

g22 confirms the gap rather than closes it: namingStanding is NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED-NOT-QUALIFIED, the harness precondition merely says runs SHOULD use machines with kexec unavailable, and it explicitly says that precondition is not cryptographic proof and does not satisfy DR-126. A non-enforced lab preference cannot prove that replacement did not occur on the machine under qualification.

Concrete counterexample: boot allowlisted K through the complete measured-boot ceremony, kexec undeclared M, and run qualification under M. The signed transcript and quote still authenticate the firmware launch of K; v32 has intentionally removed any pass/fail current-image proof. All boot-time checks can pass, buildIdDriftDetector cannot refuse, and the only record of M is a non-closing disclosure.

This is an honest repair of Claude's complaint that v31 asserted false build-ID closure, but it does not implement the trusted current-image observation or enforced no-replacement interval required by PTCB-V31-B1. Calling the residual disclosed cannot convert an actual undeclared host-ABI dependency into a closed TCB.
blockers.impact: The proposed Linux profile can accept boot-time evidence for K while the process actually depends on undeclared kernel M. The active OS-ABI TCB is not closed, NT-TCB-1/NT-TCB-3 cannot pass, and the hostile-clean-machine property remains unproved.
blockers.requiredRepair: To keep Linux in slice 1 without a deferral, authenticate the currently executing kernel through evidence rooted outside that kernel and join its cryptographic identity to the signed OS-ABI entry, or attest and enforce a monotonic no-replacement property from the measured launch through observedAt. The proof must fail closed when unavailable and be part of the qualification event. A disclosure or SHOULD-level harness precondition may remain as limitation text but cannot replace the mandatory pass/fail closure.

shouldFix.title: A live enforcedBootPolicy clause still assigns NT-TCB-KEXEC to the removed currentExecution field
evidence: v32 removes measuredBootBind.currentExecution and replaces it with optional buildIdDriftDetector, whose role expressly says a match or mismatch MUST NOT pass or fail NT-TCB-1/3. The negative-test roster replaces NT-TCB-KEXEC with the non-pass/fail NT-TCB-DISCLOSE-KEXEC cell.

The live enforcedBootPolicy.runtimeContinuity string still says: NT-TCB-KEXEC is currentExecution.gnuBuildId, not this field. currentExecution is no longer a member of the extras-rejected measuredBootBind object, and the statement directly contradicts the new non-closing standing.

runtimeContinuity.roleGoverns establishes only that runtimeContinuity is optional hardening; it does not supply or serialize the referenced currentExecution field. One validator can treat the stale sentence as an impossible mandatory cell, while another can ignore it in favor of the disclosure.
shouldFix.impact: The live policy has an undefined required reference and two incompatible descriptions of the kexec cell, causing deterministic over-refusal or inconsistent qualification records.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Delete the currentExecution/NT-TCB-KEXEC assignment from enforcedBootPolicy.runtimeContinuity and make that live sentence agree with the chosen disclosure standing: runtimeContinuity is optional hardening and no current-execution pass/fail cell exists in this generation.

shouldFix.title: The recomputeDigest exemption ambiguously removes the signedEntry join it is supposed to preserve
evidence: preKernelEventUnion.rule first requires every non-kernel codeBearing row to appear in preKernelReferences with the tagged digest join, then adds except where signed digest equality is the intended proof. recomputeDigest.rule says signed digest equality is the intended proof for every non-kernel code-bearing row. Read literally, the exception therefore removes preKernelReferences from every row for which it was meant to waive only byte recomputation.

measuredBootTranscript.codeJoin simultaneously requires every non-kernel codeBearing transcript row to join through preKernelReferences.join. The only retained signedEntry location for that relationship is the preKernelReferences row, so omitting it leaves no four-field class/identity/origin member to perform the claimed equality.

preKernelReferences.requiredFor remains limited to PCR 0/1/2/4 through the first PCR-4 separator, while the governing transcript and preKernelEventUnion now cover PCR 0/1/2/4/7 through each PCR's own separator. A PCR-7 codeBearing row is therefore required by codeJoin but omitted by the row's own requiredFor scope.

The governing equality also names only signedEntry DIGEST-BOUND digest, while preKernelReferences.join continues to admit PLATFORM-ATTESTED and compares the event digest to authenticityCore.payload.digest. The class map makes PLATFORM-ATTESTED reachable for loader, framework, and comparable system-class entries, but a package archive digest is not generally the measured PE/blob digest.
shouldFix.impact: A permissive validator can accept a code-bearing event because its digest is in the signed transcript without joining a four-field TCB member; a strict validator requires the missing row or rejects lawful evidence. PLATFORM-ATTESTED code entries also have incompatible equality rules.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Require a preKernelReferences row and four-field signedEntry join for every non-kernel codeBearing transcript row in the full five-PCR governing interval. Waive only reconstruction from preimageBytes, not the signedEntry join. Remove the exception from the appearance requirement, propagate the per-PCR interval to requiredFor, and either restrict these rows to DIGEST-BOUND identity or define a content digest in PLATFORM-ATTESTED that equals the measured code digest rather than the package archive digest.

advisories.title: g22.doesNotClaim begins with a status token that contradicts the G22 standing
evidence: g22.namingStanding and kexecHarnessPrecondition both say NAMED-NOT-QUALIFIED, and whatThisDoesNotDo says the artifact does not qualify G22.

g22.doesNotClaim nevertheless begins with the standalone token QUALIFIED. before stating the limitation. No meaning for that token is defined, and it is the sole positive qualification word in the live G22 object.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Remove QUALIFIED. from doesNotClaim or replace it with an unambiguous limitation label that cannot be read as a G22 status.

verdictBasis: REJECT because ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX; this review finds 1 blocker and 2 SHOULD-FIX findings.
conclusion: REJECT. v32 honestly demotes GNU build ID to optional non-closing metadata, restores the post-kexec limitation, unifies the five-PCR transcript interval, narrows byte recomputation, adds the missing ACTION bytes, fixes globalLogIndex, and pins one TCG PFP edition. The disclosure route still cannot close a mandatory Linux OS-ABI profile: a post-kexec kernel M is an actual host-ABI TCB member, but v32 neither observes and refuses M nor makes it inapplicable or removes Linux. One live policy still names the removed currentExecution cell, and the new recomputation exemption can waive the signedEntry row it was meant to preserve. DR-126 remains OPEN; Linux remains in D-002 slice 1; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, application, sealing, or implementation authority is created.
